title: Avocado Fat: How Much It Has, What Type, and How It Compares

seo.title: Avocado Fat: Amount and Type
seo.meta_description: Avocado provides about 14.7 g fat per 100 g, mostly monounsaturated. Compare it with olive oil, nuts, butter and other fruit.
seo.search_intent: Understand the amount and type of fat in avocado.

excerpt: Avocado contains about 14.7 g fat per 100 g: roughly 9.8 g monounsaturated, 1.8 g polyunsaturated and 2.1 g saturated. Oleic acid is the dominant fatty acid.
content_html:
Avocado is a fruit, but its nutrition label looks nothing like an apple or an orange. Those fruits contain very little fat; 100 g of avocado provides about 14.7 g fat and 160 calories.

The useful question is not simply whether avocado is “high in fat,” but what kind of fat it contains and what you are comparing it with. Roughly two-thirds of avocado fat is monounsaturated, with oleic acid as the dominant fatty acid.

What is actually in 100 grams?

Per 100 g avocadoApprox. amount
Total fat14.7 g
Monounsaturated fat~9.8 g
Polyunsaturated fat~1.8 g
Saturated fat~2.1 g
Calories160
Fiber6.7 g

Only about 2.1 g of the 14.7 g total is saturated fat. That distribution is why avocado fits more naturally among foods rich in unsaturated fats than among high-saturated-fat foods.

Oleic acid links avocado and olive oil

Both foods are rich in the same major monounsaturated fatty acid, but they are not nutritionally interchangeable. Public-health guidance favors replacing some saturated fat with unsaturated fat; avocado can help make that substitution when it replaces foods such as butter or certain creamy spreads.

Unsaturated fat still supplies energy. All dietary fat provides about 9 calories per gram, so portion size remains part of the picture.

Compared with butter, the fat profile changes dramatically

Avocado contains about 2.1 g saturated fat/100 g, while butter contains more than 50 g/100 g. Equal weights therefore differ by more than twentyfold in saturated fat.

Real servings make the comparison more useful. Ten grams of butter provides about 5 g saturated fat and 72 calories. Fifty grams of avocado provides about 1 g saturated fat and 80 calories, plus roughly 3.4 g fiber. The calories are similar, but the foods are doing very different nutritional jobs.

Compared with olive oil, water changes everything

Olive oil is essentially pure fat: about 100 g fat and 884 calories per 100 g. Avocado provides 14.7 g fat and 160 calories because roughly three-quarters of its weight is water.

One U.S. tablespoon of olive oil, about 14 g, is roughly 120 calories; 50 g avocado is about 80 calories. Oil delivers much more fat in a small volume, while avocado brings water, fiber and bulk.

Nuts are much more concentrated too

Almonds are around 50 g fat and 579 calories/100 g; walnuts around 65 g and 654 calories. Against those foods, avocado's 14.7 g fat and 160 calories look far less concentrated.

So both statements can be true: avocado is high-fat for a fruit, but relatively low in fat concentration compared with nuts or oil.

Is “healthy fat” a useful label?

It can be shorthand if the meaning is clear. Avocado's fat profile is dominated by unsaturated fats, and WHO guidance favors unsaturated over saturated fat. But the nutritional effect depends partly on what the avocado replaces.

Replacing butter with avocado changes the saturated-to-unsaturated balance. Adding avocado without replacing anything simply adds energy, even if the fat profile is favorable.

Avocado is more than its fat

One hundred grams also provides about 6.7 g fiber and roughly 485 mg potassium. That whole-food matrix is a major difference from oil, which contains no fiber and almost no water.

Portion size changes the total quickly

Avocado fleshCaloriesFat
50 g807.3 g
100 g16014.7 g
150 g24022 g

“Half an avocado” is not a very precise nutrition measure because fruit size varies widely. When the amount matters, grams are more informative than a fraction of the fruit.

The useful takeaway

Avocado fat is mostly monounsaturated. It contains far more fat than watery fruit, but far less concentrated fat than nuts or oil. Its value is not a magic “healthy fat” label; it is the combination of unsaturated fat, fiber, potassium and volume within an actual meal.

faq.question: How much fat is in avocado?
faq.answer: About 14.7 g/100 g, including roughly 9.8 g monounsaturated and 2.1 g saturated fat.

faq.question: Does avocado have more fat than nuts?
faq.answer: No. Almonds are around 50 g fat/100 g and walnuts around 65 g, versus 14.7 g in avocado.

faq.question: Is avocado fat the same as olive oil?
faq.answer: Both are rich in oleic acid, but olive oil is almost pure fat and about 884 calories/100 g versus 160 for avocado.
